items.title: George Guesnon Interview
items.q: I read in a little book kid Thomas with his enormous power he can play for 14 hours without stopping

ctx.x: Where were they playing those days?

Well, they were playing different places. I didn't go to the places they played, but I used to meet them on Sunday advertising. Oh, in the wagon. Advertising on the street, not hop on and give me a bunch of folders, or circulars in other words they call them. I would deliver them just to be out there with them, you know. Something like that hand bill of Kid Thomas? That's right, a hand bill. That's really what it was, a hand bill.
Can you tell us anything else about your family? Did your father favor you?

items.title: George Guesnon Interview, 1965-09
items.q: I was making some records across the river with Kid Thomas and Neil A. Barnes on the old American label

ctx.x: you know George Lewis in that book about him there he says that they're always when he gets on the stage he says a prayer he can't the prayer which his mother told him to say offerings to God and then he never gets there in a stage right or something like that you see see when he gets out there he pray for him

well yeah well oh you always playing for him understand this why you see right now you're a trumpet player there's so much about your horn that you don't know but there's one teacher I mean you can come to me I can help you you can go to another man he can help you but man all you do is sit down at home and say tell him your trouble tell him your trouble that's right say Lord I want it and I want it bad I really want it please help me to get over it man he'll show you things and ideas that you never dreamed of…
Like a horse. Yeah. Yeah. Yeah. That's because you're a Creole. Oh, that's right. Oh, that's right.

items.title: "Kid Thomas" Valentine Interview, 1959-12-10
items.q: it happened to George Gaynor, he wouldn't mind me telling you about it

ctx.x: Oh, here's something funny, it happened to George Gaynor, he wouldn't mind me telling you about it. One time he was broke, but he took his banjo up and pawned it. He was going to get some money and bet on the races and, oh no, here's a different than that, he was going to meet somebody for a job.
